title: 3D Magnetic Stem Cell Aggregation and Bioreactor Maturation for Cartilage Regeneration
protocol: Make micro-holes with a 0.8-mm drill through aluminum plates (3 cm in diameter and 6 mm thick).
Insert a magnetic tip (750 μm in diameter) into each hole of the plate.
Place this disk over a permanent neodymium magnet to ensure magnetization to saturation.
Cut hard polystyrene into 2.4 cm² squares.
Insert 9 small magnets (3 mm in diameter, 6 mm long) at an equal distance over a surface area of 1.6 cm².
Place this device over a permanent neodymium magnet.
Culture human mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) in complete mesenchymal stem cell growth medium (MSCGM) at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until near confluence (~90%).

Prepare a magnetic labeling solution by mixing 0.1 or 0.2 mM maghemite citrate-coated iron oxide (γFe2O3; core: 8 nm diameter) in serum-free McCoy's 5A medium modified at Roswell Park Memorial Institute (RMPI) without glutamine and containing 5 mM sodium citrate.
Discard the medium from the cell culture flask.
Rinse the cells with serum-free RPMI medium without glutamine.
Add 10 mL of iron oxide nanoparticle solution per 150-cm2 culture flask to cover all the cells.
Incubate for 30 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Discard the nanoparticle solution after incubation.
Rinse with serum-free RPMI medium without glutamine for 5 min to internalize nanoparticles still attached to the plasma membrane.
Discard RPMI medium from each flask.
Add 25 mL of complete MSCGM medium per flask.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Prepare chondrogenic medium using DMEM high glucose with L-glutamine.
Add 50 µM L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate to the medium.
Add 0.1 µM dexamethasone to the medium.
Add 1 mM sodium pyruvate to the medium.
Add 0.35 mM L-proline to the medium.
Add 1% universal culture supplement (ITS-Premix) to the medium.
Add 10 ng/mL transforming growth factor-beta 3 (TGF-β3) to the medium.
Detach magnetic cells using 8 mL of 0.05% trypsin-EDTA per 150-cm2 culture flask.
Centrifuge the dissociated cells at 260 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the medium from the centrifuged cells.
Count the re-suspended cells.
Place a glass-bottomed cell culture Petri dish on top of both magnetic devices.
Add 3 mL of chondrogenic medium to the Petri dish.
Gently deposit no more than 8 µL containing 2.5×10^5 labeled cells per aggregate (up to 16 aggregates).
Leave the Petri dish for 20-30 min without moving it.
Place the complete device, including the Petri dish with aggregates, into the incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Place 2 aggregates in contact on day 8 to form 8 doublets and initiate the fusion.
Merge 2 doublets to form 4 quadruplets on day 11.
Fuse the 4 quadruplets on day 15 to obtain the final structure.
Centrifuge 2.5×10^5 labeled stem cells at 260 × g for 5 min in 15-mL tubes with 1.5 mL of chondrogenic medium with or without TGF-β3 (for sample and control, respectively).
Place each dried scaffold into a Petri dish.
Dilute 2×10^6 labeled stem cells in 350 µL of chondrogenic medium without TGF-β3.
Pipette the cell suspension onto the scaffold carefully.
Incubate for 5 min at 37 °C to allow full cell penetration within the scaffold.
Gently add 3 mL of chondrogenic medium with or without TGF-β3 (for sample or control, respectively) to the Petri dish.
Incubate the cellularized scaffold on its magnetic device at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 4 days.
Seed scaffolds with 2×10^6 labeled stem cells following the same method and incubate without the magnet to obtain uniformly seeded scaffolds as positive controls.
Remove magnets after 4 days of incubation.
Continue chondrogenic maturation in a Petri dish under static conditions for negative control samples.
Maintain cellularized scaffolds or aggregates in the same Petri dish under static conditions.
Change chondrogenic medium twice weekly for 21 days under static conditions.
Prepare bioreactor setup according to manufacturer's protocol for dynamic conditions.
Cut silicone tubing to appropriate length as per manufacturer instructions.
Autoclave all materials including culture chamber, tubing, 2-way rotators, and cages.
Place bioreactor parts into a sterile microbiological safety station.
Connect tubing to the 2-way rotators and culture chamber according to manufacturer’s guidelines.
Transfer cellularized scaffolds into sterilized cages using a sterile spatula.
Insert two scaffolds per cage.
Secure cages in needles on lid of culture chamber to prevent movement during rotation.
Fill culture chamber with chondrogenic medium and close it with the lid containing cages.
Turn on peristaltic pump to fill tubing with chondrogenic medium and eliminate air bubbles.
Place filled chamber into motor of bioreactor and secure.
Start computer control system for rotations of arm and chamber.
Apply a rotation speed of 5 rpm on both the arm and the chamber.
Adjust the peristaltic pump at a flow rate of 10 rpm for continuous feeding of the cellularized scaffolds.
Prepare 1 mL of enzymatic solution by adding 100 µL of pullulanase (40 U/mL) and 50 µL of dextranase (60 mg/mL) to 850 µL of serum-free DMEM medium.
Rinse the scaffolds twice with serum-free DMEM medium, discard the medium.
Add 800 µL of enzymatic solution per scaffold.
Incubate for 15-30 min at 37 °C under gentle agitation.
Transfer the solution containing the cells to a 1.5-mL tube after the scaffold is completely dissolved.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min, carefully aspirate the medium.
Rinse twice with sterile 1× phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min again.
Re-suspend the cells in the RNA isolation solution.
Place the spheroids in the RNA isolation solution and completely crush them using a homogenizer.
Isolate the RNA using a kit for total RNA extraction according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Synthesize complementary DNA from 400 ng of total RNA.
Use 250-ng random primers, 1 µL of dNTP mix (10 mM each), and 40 U/mL RNase inhibitor for the reaction.
Add distilled water to reach a final volume of 100 µL after the reverse transcription reaction.
Prepare a PCR mix containing a fluorescent reagent for quantitative PCR.
Dilute cDNA by a factor of 10× for use in the PCR reactions.
Quantify relative expression levels of aggrecan (AGC) and collagen II (Col II) genes using the PCR mix.
Normalize gene expression levels with Ribosomal Protein, Large, P0 (RPLP0).
Calculate ΔCT as the CT value of the gene of interest minus the CT value of RPLP0.
Determine ΔΔCT by subtracting mean ΔCT of control condition from ΔCT of differentiated condition.
Use the 2-ΔΔCT formula to quantify relative expression levels.
Perform statistical analysis using Student's t-test for comparisons between centrifuged pellets and magnetic fusions (* p < 0.05).
Analyze data with a Kruskal-Wallis test (one-way ANOVA nonparametric) for differences between differentiated scaffolds and the control scaffold (* p < 0.05).
Rinse cellularized scaffolds or aggregates with sterile 1× PBS.
Fix samples in 10% formalin solution for 1 hour at room temperature.
Rinse fixed samples with 1× PBS.
Embed samples in optimal cutting temperature compound (OCT).
Freeze embedded samples in an isopentane bath immersed in liquid nitrogen.
Store frozen samples at -20°C.
Cut the stored samples with a cryostat to obtain 8-µm thick sections for aggregates or 12-µm thick sections for cellularized scaffolds.
Stain cryosections with 0.5% toluidine blue solution for 2 minutes.
Rinse stained sections in tap water.
Dehydrate sections with 100% ethanol.
Clarify sections using toluene.
Mount the slides with a mounting medium for light microscopy.
